page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading. It is equipped with 84.0 GB of RAM, translating to an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per core. Storage includes a 236 GB local disk, and the server is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to the high 4.2 GHz clock speed, single-core performance is strong, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching the top 10% tier and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression performing in the top 25%. However, because of the limited core count of 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs, multi-core performance is weak, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with uncached large-block read and write speeds categorized as poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4-2mds_v2 offers a highly specialized resource density. It is designed for scenarios requiring massive memory capacity without the overhead of paying for unneeded CPU cores. The primary tradeoff is the low parallel processing capability; workloads requiring high multi-threaded throughput or massive memory bandwidth will face bottlenecks. However, for applications that benefit from Intel's advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX on a single-core basis, this configuration provides targeted hardware acceleration.

This server is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded or low-concurrency workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight LLM text generation where memory capacity is critical but parallel compute demands are minimal.
